title: Proforma & billing options for multi-year prepay (1yr vs 3yr + ramp)
text:
Proforma & billing options for multi-year prepay (1yr vs 3yr + ramp)

["From: Allison Tran <allison.tran@globex.com>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: James Moore <james.moore@globex.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Budget request: multi-year prepay scenarios for FY27 planning

Hi Rafael / Monica,

We're building the FY27 budget and considering a prepay commitment for inference costs. Leadership asked for a couple of pro forma invoices we can circulate with finance: one for a 12-month prepay at an annualized discount, and one for a 3-year prepay with a ramp (year 1 smaller, year 2+3 increases).

Key asks:
- Line-item pro forma(s) showing unit pricing, year-by-year spend, and the effective discount vs pay-as-you-go
- Two billing cadence options: annual prepay vs multi-year upfront (one invoice)
- Suggested ramp schedule (example: 40% year 1, 60% year 2, 100% year 3 of projected consumption) and how unused prepay is treated
- Any minimums or termination/true-up rules we should be aware of

Target timeline: can you get draft pro formas for our FP&A review by EOD Wednesday (2026-04-14)?

Thanks,
Allison
Allison Tran
Director, Finance Operations
Globex Corp
allison.tran@globex.com

---
(Attachment requested: sample proforma + ramp assumptions)", "From: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Allison Tran <allison.tran@globex.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Budget request: multi-year prepay scenarios for FY27 planning

Allison — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching two draft pro formas and a sample ramp schedule for your FP&A team to review. High level notes below; details are in the PDFs.

Summary (high level):
- Option A — 12-month annual prepay: 15% discount vs PAYG, invoiced annually in advance. No true-up unless usage exceeds committed units; overages billed at PAYG rates monthly.
- Option B — 3-year prepay (single upfront invoice): 25% effective discount vs PAYG when amortized across 3 years. We model a ramp schedule with year-by-year committed units (40% / 60% / 100%) and credit carry-forward rules for the term.
- Billing options: we can do a single upfront invoice (preferred for finance to lock rate) or annual invoices with a pre-agreed discount schedule.
- Termination/true-up: for single upfront prepay we offer limited pro-rated refunds only in the case of force majeure; standard is credit roll-forward against future consumption within the contracted term.

Attachments included: Globex_Proforma_3yr_v2.pdf (pro forma with amortization table), Proforma_1yr_option.pdf (annual prepay). Also attaching a draft ramp_schedule.xlsx with suggested commit tiers.

Open questions for you:
1) Do you prefer single upfront invoice or annual invoicing for accounting?
2) Do you want the discount applied as an effective rate reduction or as a prepay credit bucket (we can present both)?
3) Any internal constraints on PO timing that would impact signing before your fiscal year close?

If it's helpful, I can prepare a short summary slide that ties each option to FY27 cashflow and FY28 impact.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0193

(Attachments: Globex_Proforma_3yr_v2.pdf; Proforma_1yr_option.pdf; ramp_schedule.xlsx)", 'From: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Allison Tran <allison.tran@globex.com>, rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 10:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Budget request: multi-year prepay scenarios for FY27 planning

Allison — quick note from CS/estimates on the usage profile we recommend to make the pro forma conservative but realistic. Rafael, feel free to incorporate these into the next rev.

Assumptions used in attached ramp_schedule.xlsx:
- Baseline monthly token consumption: 1.2B tokens/month (current run-rate + 15% buffer)
- Year 1 commit: 40% of projected FY27 usage (protects against over-commit while securing discount)
- Annual growth: 35% year-over-year for years 2->3 based on Globex roadmap signals
- Overages: billed monthly at PAYG, with auto-conversion to next tier if sustained >120% of committed for 3 consecutive months

Recommendations:
- For finance comfort, present both: (a) single upfront invoice with 25% effective discount and credit roll-forward policy, and (b) annual prepay with 15% discount but with a pre-agreed rollover/true-up at year-end.
- Include an appendix that models cashflow impact under three adoption curves (conservative, expected, aggressive) — I can deliver that if you want.

Laura — flagging procurement items (PO cadence) so we can align on invoice delivery format.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai

---
(Attachment: ramp_schedule.xlsx)', "From: Allison Tran <allison.tran@globex.com>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: James Moore <james.moore@globex.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 11:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Budget request: multi-year prepay scenarios for FY27 planning

Thanks Rafael / Monica — this is very helpful. FP&A reviewed and prefers the single upfront 3-year prepay structure for FY27 cash planning, but they asked for two final items before we sign:
1) A concise pro forma that shows both the invoice total (single upfront) and an amortized view for FY27/FY28/FY29 cash impact (same as your v2 PDF but condensed to one page).
2) A formal statement of the discount calculation and the credit roll-forward rules to include in our procurement packet (they need clear language on how unused prepay is handled and any refund triggers).

If you can provide those two deliverables early next week we can route the DocuSign PO to procurement. Also confirm whether Redwood can accept a Net 60 payment term on the single upfront invoice (we'd need Net 60 for our quarter-end cash management).

Next steps requested:
- Rafael: one-page amortized pro forma + discount calc language (deliver by Mon 2026-04-20 EOD)
- Laura: procurement confirmation on invoice formatting and acceptable payment terms (Net 30 vs Net 60)

We appreciate the quick turnaround — this will help us lock FY27 numbers.

Best,
Allison
Allison Tran
Director, Finance Operations
Globex Corp
